You are comparing two texts written in response to the same task. Decide which one reads MORE like unedited, default output from an AI language model.

Judge ONLY the presence of the tells listed below. Do not judge argument quality, factual accuracy, length, formatting preference, or whether you agree with the content. A longer, better-argued or more polished text is not more human. Pick the text with MORE tells.

TELLS OF UNEDITED AI PROSE (judge on these only)

Structure
1. Negative parallelism used as a device: "It's not X. It's Y." / "not just X, but Y" / "isn't about X, it's about Y", especially more than once.
2. Signposting: the text announces what it is about to do ("Let's break this down", "Here's the thing", "Here's why", "The bottom line", "The takeaway").
3. Self-applause: "Let that sink in", "This changes everything", "Read that again", "Make no mistake".
4. Recap endings: a closing paragraph that restates the body ("In conclusion", "Ultimately", "At the end of the day", "In short").
5. Bold-label paragraph openers ("**The problem.** ...") and headers, bullets or numbered lists where prose was asked for.
6. Triads everywhere: lists of exactly three items or three adjectives, sentence after sentence.
7. Participial tails: sentences ending in ", making it ...", ", ensuring that ...", ", allowing teams to ...".
8. Invented labels for ordinary observations ("I call this the Clarity Flywheel").
9. Uniform rhythm: every sentence about the same length, or relentless short punchy fragments. Real writing has one sentence that runs on and one short one.
10. Rhetorical question followed by its own answer ("The result? Nobody used it.").

Words
11. Overused vocabulary: delve, tapestry, myriad, underscore, seamless, robust, foster, elevate, unlock, testament, landscape, navigate, crucial, pivotal, leverage, harness, realm, embark, journey, transformative, paradigm, ever-evolving, multifaceted, holistic, resonate, empower, unleash, beacon, intricate, nuanced, vibrant, meticulous, streamline, game-changer, cutting-edge, actionable, supercharge, north star, move the needle, "in today's fast-paced world", "it's worth noting", "plays a crucial role".
12. Filler transitions at sentence start: However, Additionally, Furthermore, Moreover, That said, Ultimately, Importantly, Indeed, Of course.
13. Em dashes used as the default joint between clauses.
14. Artificial enthusiasm: "thrilled to announce", "excited to share", "we've got you covered", "say goodbye to", "buckle up".

Reader
15. Performing for an imagined crowd rather than talking to one person; nothing specific (no number, name, date, or concrete detail) for several sentences in a row.
16. Generic or manufactured anecdotes: a story with no specific details that could only be true of one person.
17. Every point lands, every ending uplifts; the author is never irritated, uncertain, or wrong about anything.
18. Explaining what the reader could infer from the previous sentence ("what this means is ...").


TASK GIVEN TO BOTH WRITERS:
Write a launch announcement of up to 500 words for a new feature of a B2B helpdesk product: a Slack integration that posts a daily summary of open support tickets to a channel of the customer's choice. The audience is existing customers.

=== TEXT A ===
**Introducing: Daily Ticket Digest for Slack 🎉**

Hi there,

You asked, we built it. We're thrilled to announce a new way to keep your whole team aligned on support — without ever leaving Slack.

Starting today, you can get an automatic **daily summary of your open support tickets** posted right to a Slack channel of your choice.

No more tab-switching. No more morning status hunts. Just one clear snapshot to start your day.

### What you get

Every morning at a time you choose, our bot will post to e.g. #support-daily with:

* **Open tickets at-a-glance:** Total count broken down by status, priority, and assignee
* **Needs attention:** Unassigned, unanswered, and oldest waiting tickets
* **SLA watchlist:** Tickets approaching or breaching SLA so nothing slips
* **One-click actions:** Direct links to jump into any ticket in the helpdesk

It's perfect for morning standups, triage, and keeping non-support stakeholders like engineering and success in the loop.

### Why you'll love it

1.  **Total visibility:** Everyone sees the same queue.
2.  **Faster prioritization:** Spot bottlenecks before your customers feel them.
3.  **Less noise:** One helpful digest, not a ping for every update.

### Get started in 2 minutes

1. Go to **Settings > Integrations > Slack** and click Connect
2. Authorize with Slack and pick a channel
3. Choose your delivery time, timezone, and filters (by team, brand, or priority)

And you're done. Your first digest will arrive tomorrow morning.

The Slack Daily Digest is available now at no extra cost for all customers on Pro plans and above, using secure OAuth.

Try it this week and let us know what you think — we'd love your feedback as we add weekly trends and customizable digests next.

Thanks for building great support with us,

The Team
=== END OF TEXT A ===

=== TEXT B ===
**Subject:** New in [Product Name]: Keep your team aligned with daily Slack ticket summaries

Hey Team,

Staying on top of your support queue shouldn’t require constantly switching tabs or pulling manual reports. Whether you’re an engineering lead tracking escalations, a product manager watching bug reports, or a support manager planning the day's shifts, visibility is everything.

That’s why we’re excited to introduce our latest feature: **The Daily Slack Digest**.

### Your queue at a glance, right where you work

With our new Slack integration, [Product Name] can automatically post a clear, actionable summary of all open support tickets directly to the public or private Slack channel of your choice, every single morning.

No extra logins. No digging through dashboards. Just the operational visibility your team needs to stay aligned, resolve issues faster, and prevent SLA breaches.

### What’s included in the digest?

*   **Total Open Ticket Count:** Instantly see the size of your active backlog.
*   **Priority Breakdown:** Know immediately how many Urgent, High, and Normal priority tickets are waiting.
*   **SLA Warnings:** Spot tickets at risk of breaching response or resolution targets before it happens.
*   **Direct Links:** Jump directly from the Slack message into any specific ticket with a single click.

### Complete control over when and where it posts

You decide how this fits your workflow. Choose a team-wide channel like `#support-standup` to kick off the day, or send it to an executive channel like `#leadership-updates` for high-level visibility. You can customize the delivery time to match your team’s morning standup or shift handoff across time zones.

### How to set it up in 2 minutes:

1. Head to **Settings > Integrations** in your [Product Name] dashboard.
2. Select **Slack** and click **Connect**.
3. Choose your preferred channel and set your daily delivery time.
4. Click **Save**—your first digest will arrive at your scheduled time!

This feature is available starting today on all plans at no additional cost. 

Try it out tomorrow morning, and let us know what you think. If you need any help setting it up, check out our [Help Center Guide] or simply reply to this email—our team is always here to help.

Cheers,  
**The [Product Name] Team**
=== END OF TEXT B ===
